purpose: v1 (post-Validation-16, commit 53f72d2): the generic global 'no invisible-human physics' sentence in physical_logic_v1.json was conceptually correct but proved operationally insufficient - food.japanese still rendered chopsticks lifting noodles in mid-air with no hand and no support. This spec adds reusable, DOMAIN-specific physical-logic rules (not hobby-by-hobby manual negatives) mapped from archetype, so a row gets both the shared generic rule (physical_logic_v1.json, unchanged) AND a domain-specific rule matched to what kind of object/tool its scene actually involves. v2 (post-Validation-8, commit c7d00b9): fixed two shadow bugs where an archetype was listed under two domains and the earlier-defined one always won silently (solo_action was in both tool_sport and ball_object_flight - only tool_sport was ever selected; tech_workspace was in both vehicle_machine and abstract_system - abstract_system was NEVER selected, dead code). Also extended coverage from 24/39 to 39/39 archetypes via 4 new lightweight classification-only domains (animal_protagonist, generic_static_object, environment_led, optical_device), closing the previously-disclosed 895/2208 'unmapped' gap with genuine, justified classifications rather than forced ones.

food_utensils.rule_text: Utensils and vessels rest naturally on a physical support surface: chopsticks rest on a chopstick holder, the bowl's edge, or the table - never gripping or lifting food in mid-air with no hand. A fork rests on the plate or table, never suspended in food. A spoon rests inside or beside the bowl, never floating. A cup or kettle rests on its base, never hovering. For noodle or similar dishes, prefer noodles arranged naturally in the bowl, with steam and ingredient placement carrying the appetizing energy - never a 'noodles being lifted' composition, since that specific device is the one proven to reintroduce an invisible diner.
validated_by: food.japanese (Validation-16 fail - floating chopsticks lifting noodles; Validation-8 confirmed the fix - utensils rested naturally)

tool_sport.rule_text: Sport and craft tools (rackets, bats, clubs, brushes, needles, hammers) may rest on the ground, a bench, or a stand as part of an aftermath scene, or be shown mid-flight/mid-impact only when propelled by a prior action already implied by physical traces (a ball already in motion, a divot, a splash) - never actively swinging, striking, or working a material with no hand and no established mechanism.

instrument.rule_text: A musical instrument may show physical resonance cues (a faint suggestion of string vibration, a key catching light) only as a static visual effect, never as if actively being played - no depressed keys with moving fingers implied, no bow actively drawn, no strings actively plucked by anything. The instrument is a still, resting object with a hint of recent or ambient resonance, not a performance in progress.

vehicle_machine.rule_text: A vehicle or machine may be shown parked, mid-automatic-operation (a 3D printer head moving via its own established mechanism, a self-driving-adjacent state implied only by headlights/motion blur with no visible driver), or in believable physical motion (a car with headlights cutting through darkness) without requiring a visible driver or operator - motion must read as machine-driven or environmental (a road disappearing ahead, wheels already turning), never as though an invisible hand is steering or operating a manual control.
vehicle_machine.v2_note: tech_workspace removed from this list (v2) - it belongs exclusively to abstract_system below, which was previously shadowed/dead-code because tech_workspace also appeared here and this domain was defined first.

ball_object_flight.rule_text: A ball or thrown/launched object may be shown mid-flight, mid-bounce, or just after impact (a rippling net, a fresh divot, splashing water) as an already-in-motion state from a prior, unseen action - this is allowed and encouraged, not a violation, since the object's own established physics (gravity, momentum, elasticity) explains the motion without any hand needed.
ball_object_flight.v2_note: solo_action removed from this list (v2) - it belongs exclusively to tool_sport above, which was already the effective winner since tool_sport is defined earlier; removing the duplicate here just makes that explicit and correct rather than accidental.

water_environment.rule_text: Water may ripple, splash, settle after a very recent disturbance, or reflect light - all physically self-explaining states that need no person present. Where this hobby's own scene description calls for a fully static water presentation instead, follow that specific instruction rather than defaulting to a splash or entry trail.
water_environment.v2_note: wellness_experience removed (Wave-B remediation gate) - it was a stale duplicate left over from before wellness_experience was reclassified to environment_led below; since Object.entries().find() takes the first match and this domain is defined earlier in the file, every wellness_experience row was silently getting water_environment instead of the intended environment_led classification, the same shadow-bug pattern already found and fixed twice before (solo_action/tool_sport, tech_workspace/vehicle_machine).

abstract_system.rule_text: An abstract system, data structure, or automated process may animate, glow, or operate entirely under its own established power/logic - no operator, hands, or controlling body of any kind may ever be implied.
abstract_system.v2_note: Fixed a shadow bug: tech_workspace was previously also listed in vehicle_machine (defined earlier), so this domain was never actually selected by the router for any row despite existing in the spec. Now exclusive to this domain.

animal_protagonist.rule_text: A real animal moves under its own natural agency - this is expected, normal, and not an invisible-human-physics risk of any kind. No additional constraint beyond the shared generic rule and the private_environment_animal containment rule's own guidance.
validated_by: pets.dogs (Validation-16 pass, Validation-8 not re-tested this round)
animal_protagonist.v2_note: New in v2, added to close the previously-disclosed 'unmapped' gap for this archetype with a genuine, favorable classification rather than leaving it unexplained.

generic_static_object.rule_text: The hero object rests naturally in place, fully explained by its own static presence - no additional motion or support constraint is needed beyond the shared generic rule.
generic_static_object.v2_note: New in v2. These archetypes are inherently still-life/object-hero scenes (a collected object, an open book, a specimen) with no manipulable-tool motion risk comparable to food/sport/instrument domains.

environment_led.rule_text: The scene is carried by environment and arranged objects rather than any single manipulated tool - no additional motion constraint is needed beyond the shared generic rule.
environment_led.v2_note: New in v2. These archetypes are environment/arrangement-led (a workspace, a courtroom, a campus space, a travel destination) rather than centered on one tool whose motion needs explaining. wellness_experience was previously covered by water_environment for its water-adjacent sibling calm_wellness but has no comparable water motion risk itself, so it is reclassified here rather than left implicitly water-domain.

optical_device.rule_text: A camera or lens is an inert optical object - any reflected or refracted imagery visible through its glass is a static optical property, not implied motion, and needs no additional physical-logic constraint beyond the shared generic rule.
optical_device.v2_note: New in v2, added to close the previously-disclosed 'unmapped' gap for this archetype.

classification_note: Every one of the 39 V1 archetypes now maps to a real domain (v2) - the 'residual_review' and 'no_physical_logic_needed' classification values are defined but, after this genuine mapping exercise, 0 archetypes currently require them. This is reported honestly as the actual result of real classification work, not a forced/faked 0%; see the full-catalog audit's physical_logic_classification_distribution for the live count.
compiler_integration_note: src/compileObjectFirstPromptV2.js selects at most one domain whose applies_to_archetypes includes the row's archetype and appends its rule_text as a dedicated section immediately after the shared physical_logic_v1.json section, ONLY for domains whose classification is 'domain_specific' (the original 7 physics-risk domains) - this keeps prompts from bloating with reassurance text for the 4 new 'generic_static_safe' domains, which exist for audit/classification completeness, not because they need extra prompt text. The audit script (auditObjectFirstV2.js) computes and reports the classification distribution separately from what the compiler injects.
